name: Reshmi Kabab
description: Soft Pakistani reshmi kabab made from chilled chicken mince, cream, yogurt, herbs and mild spices, shaped evenly on skewers and grilled until juicy.
method: Keep the chicken mince cold while preparing the mixture. Combine it with cream, thick yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, green chillies, coriander, cumin, white pepper, garam masala and salt.
Add the lightly roasted gram flour and mix thoroughly until the mince becomes tacky and cohesive enough to hold around a skewer.
Cover and chill the mixture in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. If it still feels very loose after chilling, review its moisture rather than simply making very thick kababs.
With damp or lightly oiled hands, press the cold mixture evenly around skewers, keeping each kabab a similar moderate thickness.

Cook over a preheated grill or lightly oiled grill pan at medium-high heat, turning carefully after the surface begins to set. Continue until browned and fully cooked through; use a reliable doneness check for minced chicken.
Rest briefly so the delicate kababs firm slightly, then serve hot with mint chutney, sliced onion and lemon.
tips: Keep the mixture cold so the soft kababs hold their shape better.
Do not make the kababs excessively thick; even thickness helps the centre cook safely without drying the outside.
storage: Cool cooked kababs promptly and refrigerate covered.
image_alt: Pakistani reshmi kabab made with chilled chicken mince, cream, yogurt and mild spices
image_caption: Soft chicken reshmi kababs shaped from a chilled cohesive mince mixture and grilled until juicy.
technique: The mixture needs to stay cold and cohesive. Thick yogurt, a modest amount of cream and lightly roasted gram flour help bind the mince, but chilling does most of the shaping work without making the kababs bready.
doneness_cues: Mixture should feel tacky and hold to a skewer after chilling.
Kababs should be similar thickness from end to end.
Exterior should brown lightly without splitting apart.
Minced chicken centre must be fully cooked while remaining juicy.
mistakes: Adding too much yogurt or cream.
Using enough gram flour to make the texture dense.
Turning skewers before the surface has set.
substitutions: Use a grill pan if outdoor grilling is unavailable.
White pepper keeps the seasoning mild; black pepper changes the colour and aroma slightly.
If the mixture is soft, chill longer before adding extra binder.
reheating: Warm briefly until hot through; prolonged reheating dries the delicate mince.
serving: Serve with mint chutney, onion and lemon.
